decisions.decision: Old phase folders were intentionally discarded.
decisions.rationale: The user deleted them because they were too noisy; recreated folders do not inherit stale verification.

decisions.decision: Phase01A storage foundation lands before Hub wiring.
decisions.rationale: Migration and repository contract can be verified independently before touching channel/chat runtime behavior.

decisions.decision: Run execution facts use SQLite `runs` snapshots plus append-only `run_events`.
decisions.rationale: This follows ADR-019 and preserves cache/logs as non-canonical support planes.

decisions.decision: The Hub lifecycle store seam is optional and stores metadata-level lifecycle events only.
decisions.rationale: This keeps existing adapter delivery behavior stable while preventing raw prompts, channel data, and raw loop errors from becoming default stored event payloads.

decisions.decision: Hub persists tool/usage/final-output metadata with an allowlist.
decisions.rationale: PRD Phase 1A requires durable tool names, call ids, argument keys, status, timing, usage, and final output without raw argument values or raw tool result payloads by default.

decisions.decision: Phase01B first slice is schema plus `internal/identity`, not direct channel rewiring.
decisions.rationale: The source audit found auth, Telegram, cron, swarm, and tool allowlists all depend on the same missing authority boundary; landing schema/default-deny Authorize first prevents broad cross-surface churn.
Migration/identity tests, targeted build/vet, repo-wide build/vet, and full Go tests pass.

decisions.decision: Phase01B1 closed first, then later Phase01B slices closed the parent.
decisions.rationale: Subagent goal verifier returned PASS 10/10 for Phase01B1 only, and code-risk recheck returned PASS 9.5/10 with no B1 blockers. Later Phase01B slices closed B2-B7, fail-closed runtime paths, actor persistence, provider-secret repair, and the live marker.

decisions.decision: Phase01B2 backfills persisted Telegram allowlist identity without removing `allowed_users`.
decisions.rationale: Migration v8 backfills real persisted `allowed_users` rows into deterministic Telegram principals, channel accounts, session actors, and grants; auth bootstrap/approval creates the same rows for newly allowed users. E2E bootstrap rows remain excluded from real-user identity backfill.

decisions.decision: Phase01B3 gates dashboard `/chat` on bearer actor context plus `api.chat`.
decisions.rationale: Bearer auth now injects the deterministic Telegram session actor ID, `/chat` rejects authenticated body `user_id` overrides, and the identity authorizer records allow/deny decisions before chat execution.

decisions.decision: Phase01B3 is container E2E verified without mutating live grants.
decisions.rationale: The live container was rebuilt/recreated, bearer chat returned the exact E2E marker with one LLM call and zero tool calls, SQL recorded an `api.chat` allow decision, and destructive live missing-grant mutation was intentionally avoided because the Go test already covers that failure mode.

decisions.decision: Phase01B4 gates registry tool execution on identity capabilities when an authorizer is present.
decisions.rationale: Tool definitions now carry `RequiredCapability`, defaulting to `tool.execute`; tools may require `tool.execute.<tool_name>`. The registry calls `identity.Authorize` before `Tool.Execute`, records deny/allow decisions through the identity store, and fails closed when no identity authorizer is present.

decisions.decision: Phase01B5 ensures Telegram identity/grants before token issuance while preserving allowlist parity.
decisions.rationale: The configured allowlist remains DB/settings-backed configuration and is not copied into `allowed_users`; persisted bootstrap/approved users derive identity from stored source. Token minting now fails closed if the deterministic Telegram principal/channel-account/session-actor/grants cannot be prepared.

decisions.decision: Phase01B6 delegates cron and swarm child execution under bounded child actors.
decisions.rationale: `identity.DelegateActor` authorizes every requested child capability against the parent actor before creating direct child grants; cron manual/Hub jobs and swarm workers use the delegated actor context when identity authority is present, while Phase 8 RunGraph/topology work remains out of scope.

decisions.decision: Phase01B7 records authorization denials as metadata-only run/audit evidence.
decisions.rationale: `identity.Authorize` keeps `authz_decisions` authoritative while a narrow denial recorder appends correlated `authorization_denied` run and audit events through the Phase01A run store. Payloads include decision/capability/resource metadata, not raw prompts, tool arguments, tool outputs, request bodies, or tokens.

decisions.decision: Phase01B missing-authority runtime paths fail closed.
decisions.rationale: Registry execution now denies when no authorizer is present; cron manual jobs, cron Hub jobs, and swarm delegated assignments fail before runner execution when identity delegation is missing; app startup returns an error instead of falling back to a cron agent dispatch path if cron Hub construction fails.

decisions.decision: Phase01B parent closure is complete after the provider-secret repair.
decisions.rationale: The closure verifier passed Phase01B package gates, repo build/vet/test, container rebuild, live auth-boundary probes, Chat Hub actor persistence, DB/secrets provider repair, runtime .env removal, and exact live chat markers.

decisions.decision: Runtime provider credentials are DB/secrets-backed, not .env-backed.
decisions.rationale: Dashboard writes for keys overlaid by applySecretsToConfig now route through secrets.Store; the live stale settings.LLM_API_KEY row was removed, no .env* file remains in D:/Aura/data, and Aura chat succeeded after container rebuild without loading .env.

decisions.decision: D:/tmp/cli-printing-press is an Aura reference map, not an executable queue.
decisions.rationale: Aura adopts the workflow patterns for lean skills, machine/human output separation, and explicit shipcheck blocks while rejecting the generator/public-library flow as a canonical route.
